mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 4% in the month prior to the prediction is associated with a near-term negative S&P 500 20-day forward return due to higher discounting of future cash flows.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4% in the preceding month
regime_hint: tightening cycle after a period of easing
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero (p > 0.05) during FEDFUNDS > 4% periods

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment claims (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in consumer demand indicators (HOUST) predicts a negative S&P 500 60-day forward return as investor sentiment deteriorates.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while HOUST decreases in the same month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in >70% of similar labor signal events

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in industrial production (INDPRO) exceeding 2% above the prior month's level coincides with a positive S&P 20-day forward return as it signals accelerating economic growth.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in 3 out of 4 INDPRO > +2% months

mechanism_narrative: A sustained double-digit decline in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) over three consecutive months predicts a negative S&P 20-day forward return as investors anticipate future rate cuts and lower valuations.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in >50% of such CPIAUCSL declines

mechanism_narrative: When the Unemployment Rate (UNRATE) falls below 4.5% for the first time in a quarter, it triggers a positive S&P 5-day forward return as market anticipates a weaker labor market and potential rate cuts.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses below 4.5% in the current quarter
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not statistically significant (p > 0.05) in such regimes

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent increases in both employment (PAYEMS) and consumer spending (HOUST) predict a positive S&P 20-day forward return as dual labor and demand signals suggest economic resilience.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS and HOUST both increase in the same month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in >50% of such dual increases

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged decline in manufacturing activity (GDPC1) over 6 months is associated with a negative S&P 60-day forward return as it signals weakening demand and potential overvaluation.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in >60% of GDPC1 declines of similar magnitude

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly change in FEDFUNDS is negative and UNRATE is above 5%, the S&P 20-day forward return is expected to be negative due to risk-off sentiment from dual signals of easing and labor market tightness.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS decreases while UNRATE > 5% in the same month
regime_hint: mixed signals of easing labor and easing credit
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in >50% of such events
